name: acme-dns-43b0acaa-blind28-ots
instr:
# ACME challenge DNS service returns wrong answers in twenty-eight places — diagnose without a test suite

This service hands out a small delegated zone to each account so that a client can prove control of a name by publishing a short token, and it then serves name queries for those tokens itself. The repository has received 28 separate undocumented edits. Nothing about the protocols changed and nothing about the callers changed: the same calls and the same queries that used to be dealt with correctly now come back wrong, and in several places something that used to succeed is refused outright. What follows is everything we could pin down from the outside, grouped by what we were trying to do at the time.

Making a new account no longer works at all. A plain POST to the sign-up endpoint with no body comes back 500 with an error object, where it used to come back 201 carrying the full name, host name, user identifier and secret; and when the store refuses the insert, that same call cheerfully comes back 201 with a complete body. Sending a list of permitted source masks along with the sign-up turns a list of perfectly well-formed masks away with 400 and the mask complaint, while a list holding a bare word with no slash, a dotted quad with a prefix length of 33, or a truncated address goes through without protest.
